migration0058Status.evidence: alembic_version on the live database reads exactly ['0057_ratchet_telemetry'], read through the same ORM inside the production container. 0058 is not in the chain.
migration0058Status.reasoningVerifiedAtSource: I did not take the reasoning on faith — I queried pg_constraint and information_schema on the live database. identifier_index carries exactly TWO constraints, identifier_index_pkey (PRIMARY KEY (id)) and uq_identifier_index_type_val (UNIQUE (identifier_type, identifier_value)). The CHECK-constraint list is EMPTY, so there is no domain constraint to violate and identifier_type='cik' writes fine today. The column is character varying(8), and 'cik' is 3 characters, so it fits.
migration0058Status.futureApplyIsSafeForTheseRows: Two independent reasons. (1) 0058 adds the constraint NOT VALID on PostgreSQL, which by definition does not scan existing rows, so the 7 rows written today cannot be scanned by it. (2) Even under a full VALIDATE, 'cik' is an enumerated member of the domain 0058 declares, so these rows would pass anyway.
migration0058Status.sequenceState: identifier_index.id defaults to nextval('identifier_index_id_seq'), and the sequence last_value was 168 before the write, consistent with max(id)=168.
migration0058Status.notApplied: I did not apply 0058 and did not run alembic. It stays deploy-coupled for a soak-safe window.

remaining: STOPPED AS INSTRUCTED. The remaining 181 CIKs were NOT applied. The current plan for them is 181 issuer nodes and 261 links, 0 to retire — a separate operator decision.

OPERATOR DECISION OWED on the duplicate-active-node pattern, which is the most useful thing this run surfaced. AAPL, SPY and QQQ each have TWO active security nodes (one venue-less, one XNAS/ARCX) while SEC lists a single ticker, so the bound guardrail refused the second link for each. Extrapolated across a full run this will leave a share of securities without a trusted issuer purely because a duplicate node exists. The fix is node dedup (merge_links already exists and dedup_provisional_nodes already ships), not a looser bound — loosening the bound would re-admit the collapse the guardrail exists to stop. Recommend running the dedup for these venue-less duplicates BEFORE the remaining 181.

OPERATOR DECISION OWED on QQQ's index_concurrence 'differs'. QQQ's legacy issuer node was clean and the cohort inference still designates it, while the index now names the freshly minted node. Under MINT FRESH that is correct, but it means QQQ's security carries both an unlabelled legacy link to the old node and a cik-exact link to the new one, and the old node still exists. That duplicate-issuer state is the predicted consequence of the no-adopt ruling and will occur for all 14 remaining adoptable CIKs.

GOOG, GOOGM and GOOGN have no security nodes at all, so the Alphabet issuer node holds one link where SEC's bound is 4. If those share classes are expected to be tradable in the master, that is a universe-ingest gap rather than an identity gap, and it is not fixable by this rebuild.

Migration 0058 remains UNAPPLIED, deliberately. Note that the 7 cik rows now in production were written WITHOUT it, which confirms the column's bare String(8) accepts them; when 0058 eventually rides a deploy its NOT VALID clause will skip these rows.
The 8,334 legacy unlabelled links are all still present and still untrusted, exactly as ruled. Nothing in this run reduced that number and no ruling on retiring them was taken.

The full post-apply --all report (744KB, including all 104 disagreements and 935 guardrail violations) was pulled to the local scratchpad but is not committed anywhere durable. If the full detail is wanted for the remaining-181 decision it should be regenerated with --json-out to a retained path.
